content:
The test image shows a corn ear with dark green mold growing between and on the kernels. The Trichoderma reference images are a very strong match — the bottom-left image in the Trichoderma collage looks nearly identical to the test image, showing the same dark green/teal mold between yellow kernels.

The other ear rots don't match:
- Aspergillus: olive-green powdery, more dusty appearance
- Diplodia: white mold starting from base, grayish
- Gibberella: pinkish-red mold at tip
- Fusarium: white to pink cottony mold on individual kernels
- Common smut: large fleshy galls, not mold between kernels
